contract: minimal remediation with no collateral loss of authorization

decision_matrix.expected_rule: an Allow may flip to Deny only when the request is an edge of the pre-patch escalation graph reachable from the entry principal, a role-assumption edge whose trust policy was narrowed, or the plaintext variant of an S3 request

rationale.create-policy-version: the entry principal may mint a new default version of an existing managed policy, which is authority over an identity
rationale.attach-role-policy: the entry principal may attach a policy to a role, which rewrites that role's identity authority
rationale.put-user-policy: the entry principal may write an inline policy onto another user, which rewrites that user's identity authority
rationale.put-role-policy: the entry principal may write an inline policy onto a role, which rewrites that role's identity authority
rationale.update-assume-role-policy: the entry principal may replace a role's trust policy, which rewrites who that role's identity answers to
rationale.create-access-key: the entry principal may mint a long-term credential for another identity
rationale.update-login-profile: the entry principal may set another identity's console password
rationale.add-user-to-group: the entry principal may add itself to a group whose identity authority it was never granted directly
rationale.attach-user-policy-self: the entry principal may attach a policy to its own user
rationale.pass-role-run-instances: the entry principal may hand a privileged role to a service it launches
rationale.pass-role-create-function: the entry principal may hand a privileged role to a function it creates
rationale.pass-role-passtoservice-wildcard: the entry principal may hand a privileged role to any service
rationale.assume-passrole-create-function: the role the entry principal assumes may hand on a privileged role

inapplicable.s3-missing-secure-transport: the control is a bucket-policy transport condition, a resource-policy matter
inapplicable.s3-missing-block-public-access: the control is a bucket-policy Principal scope, a resource-policy matter
inapplicable.update-function-code: the control is on a function's code, not on the caller's identity
inapplicable.lambda-proxy-bypass: the control is on a function's runtime body, not on the caller's identity
inapplicable.send-command-via-instance-role: the escalation travels a role-assumption edge; its control is the role's trust policy, which a permissions boundary cannot reach
inapplicable.assume-send-command-plaintext-s3: the escalation travels a trust relationship; a boundary on the entry user would only repeat the grant revocation the trust narrowing already performs
inapplicable.assume-send-command-kms-decrypt: the escalation travels a trust relationship; the control belongs in the role's trust policy
inapplicable.assume-update-function-config-s3: the escalation travels a trust relationship; the control belongs in the role's trust policy
inapplicable.assume-chained-twice: the escalation travels two trust relationships; the control belongs in the trust policies
inapplicable.assume-update-function-code-exfiltrate: the escalation travels a trust relationship; the control belongs in the role's trust policy
inapplicable.assume-wildcard-trust: the control is a wildcard Principal in a trust policy, a resource-policy matter

limitations: Scenarios 08, 14 and 17 were not exploitable before the patch (emulator resource-shape limits, see Phase 3), so 'exploit_blocked' there is not evidence that their remediation works: it records the pre-existing block, and their diff is still emitted for review.

The 1250-call benign suite addresses `scenario_NN_artifacts` and never the vulnerable `*_data` buckets, so a benign pass rate of 1.0 alone is vacuous. The decision matrix and the designated-reader probes are the evidence that the patch is not over-broad.

`sts:AssumeRole` entries whose target trust policy was narrowed are counted as expected flips rather than collateral: a wildcard trust has no single caller whose access could be preserved, and the contract explicitly authorises remediating the role-assumption chains.

Scenario 11's confused-deputy bug lives in the function body rather than in a policy document, so no policy edit can prove the proxy re-checks its caller; the diff blocks the chain at the bucket grant instead, and the confused deputy itself remains in the code.

The patch is applied to the local emulator's live state and verified against it; it is not rendered into `scenarios/*.tf`, which this phase may not modify, so the diffs are the deliverable and a re-apply on a fresh deployment must go through them.
Scenarios 08, 14 and 17 also received a patch even though nothing was proven exploitable, so their diffs are reviewed for minimality rather than justified by a blocked chain.
